Maria: Heads-up — after the 23:00 deploy we saw a new all-to-all latency mode during MoE inference. peak tails at ~320ms vs usual 80-120ms.
Ajay: saw it too. single-host TPU? or inter-node NVLink knobs?
Chris: Investigating network counters now. NVLink bw looks fine, but PCIe p2p queueing spikes align with the tails.
PerfBot: perf-run #472 completed. attached flame: /perf/runs/472/stack.html
Maria: Uploading trace snippet. key points: large token bursts cause skewed token routing — one expert receives ~3x the samples for short windows.
Sophie: That could explain hot GPU kernel queuing. Which kernel path is that expert taking? fp16 vs int8?
Ajay: It's taking the standard attention + fused FFN path (fp16). We recently toggled kernel selector to prefer the 'generic' fused kernel for sequence_len>1024.
Liam: Can you paste the profiling lines? small snippet is fine.
Maria: ```
[profile] step=1203 all2all.lat: p95=312.4ms p99=451.1ms
[profile] expert A load=0.68, expert B load=0.22, expert C load=0.10
[profile] kernel=fused_ffn_generic seq=1150 batch=8
```
Chris: Look at KV cache behavior — bursts also trigger cache misses because we allocate per-token contexts then evict/rehydrate.
Sophie: Eviction thrash + routing skew = comp overlap impossible. We might be blocking on all-reduce at end of shard update.
Ajay: Hypothesis: kernel selector chooses a higher-latency path under skewed per-expert batch sizes. Need to prefer single-threaded small-batch kernels for hot experts.
Maria: Agree. Quick experiment: force fused_ffn_small for experts with sample_count<128 and measure.
PerfBot: starting job: moe-hotspot-experiment-23 force_kernel=fused_ffn_small
Liam: Also try increasing overlap window for all-reduce: async all-reduce start earlier (after partial compute) — see if comm/compute overlap improves.
Chris: FYI NCCL trace shows long wait in all2all scheduling when one participant lags. wavefront stalls 12-14x longer in skewed slices.
Sophie: Another mitigation: soft-randomize token-to-expert assignment for first 4 tokens to smooth bursts, then deterministic mapping. Cheap and might reduce instantaneous skew.
Ajay: Good idea. We can implement a small modulo jitter in router: new_index = (hash(token_id)+rand%K)%E for first N tokens.
Maria: Plan: 1) run kernel-forcing experiment, 2) enable async all-reduce overlap, 3) soft-randomize router. Run A/B on a small shard for 2 hours. Roll back if latency increases.
Liam: I'll own the async all-reduce patch. Chris will fetch nccl perf counters. Sophie will prototype router jitter. Maria/Ajay run experiments and collect perfbot outputs.
Chris: grabbing nvprof and NCCL logs now. ETA 45m.
Maria: Thanks — please annotate traces with step ids. we'll reconvene with results in ~2h. :eyes:
Ajay: noted. if anyone hits a blocking reproduce, ping me in here and tag @Ajay
Sophie: adding an eval to track quality drift for router jitter — make sure we don't degrade expert specialization.
PerfBot: job moe-hotspot-experiment-23 completed: delta p95=-27ms p99=-62ms for kernel change alone. full results pending.
Maria: Nice start. Keep updates in thread.
